title: Bonjour! Greetings and politeness
goal: Greet people at any time of day, ask how they are, say please and thank you, and choose between tu and vous.

items.note: The safe greeting for everyone, from morning until early evening.
Use it when you arrive somewhere in the evening, from about 6 p.m.
Only with friends, family and people your age. The t is silent.

items.en: How are you? / How's it going? (informal)
items.note: The answer uses the same words: Ça va ! (I'm fine!)
Polite: for people you don't know well, at work, or for more than one person.

items.en: two ways to say “you”: tu (friend) and vous (polite or plural)

drills.prompt: You meet your new landlord for the first time. How do you ask how he is?
drills.explain: A landlord is not a friend: use the polite vous form.

drills.prompt: You are talking to two friends at the same time. How do you say “And you?”
drills.explain: Vous is always used for more than one person, even friends.
With madame (polite), say s'il vous plaît.

blocks.title: Morning, at a community centre in Montréal
blocks.context: Raj, a newcomer, arrives at the front desk. Lucie works there.

lines.speaker: Lucie
lines.en: Very well, thank you. And you?

blocks.title: Evening, two friends at a café

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.fr: Ça va bien, merci. Et toi ?

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.fr: Bon, au revoir, Alex ! À bientôt !
lines.en: Well, goodbye, Alex! See you soon!

blocks.body: Play each line and listen first. Notice: Raj and Lucie are polite (**vous**), Alex and Sofia are friends (**toi**).

blocks.title: Greetings change with the time and the person
blocks.body:
- [[Bonjour]] is your all-day greeting. It works with everyone: a bus driver, a doctor, a friend.
- [[Bonsoir]] replaces bonjour when you **arrive** somewhere in the evening (from about 6 p.m.).
- [[Salut]] means both *hi* and *bye*, but **only with friends**.
- [[Au revoir]] is *goodbye*; [[À bientôt]] is *see you soon*.

Add [[monsieur]] (sir) or [[madame]] (madam) to sound polite: [[Bonjour, madame.]] This is very normal in French, not old-fashioned.

blocks.title: Tu or vous? Two ways to say “you”
blocks.body:
English has one *you*. French has two:

- **tu**: one person you know well: a friend, a family member, a child.
- **vous**: one person you don't know well (a shop clerk, your boss, an older stranger), **or** any group of two or more people.

The little words around them change too: [[s'il te plaît]] / [[s'il vous plaît]], [[Et toi ?]] / [[Et vous ?]].

**Tip:** when you are not sure, choose **vous**. It is never rude. People will tell you if they want **tu**.

blocks.title: Asking how someone is
blocks.pattern: Ça va ? → Ça va ! · Comment allez-vous ? → Très bien, merci. Et vous ?
blocks.note: [[Ça va ?]] is relaxed: with a rising voice it is a question, with a falling voice it is the answer. [[Comment allez-vous ?]] is polite.

examples.fr: Ça va ? — Ça va, merci. Et toi ?
examples.en: How's it going? — Fine, thanks. And you?

examples.fr: Comment allez-vous ? — Très bien, merci. Et vous ?
examples.en: How are you? — Very well, thank you. And you?

blocks.body:
- [[bonjour]]: the *on* is a **nasal vowel**: say “oh” and let air go through your nose. Don't pronounce an n. The *j* sounds like the *s* in “measure”.
- The French **r** is made at the back of the throat, like a soft gargle: [[bonsoir]], [[merci]], [[au revoir]].
- [[merci]] sounds like “mair-see”, not “mur-see”.
- [[s'il vous plaît]] sounds like “seel voo pleh”: the *s* of vous and the *t* of plaît are **silent**.
- [[salut]]: the *t* is silent too. You will practise the *u* sound in lesson 3.
- [[ça]]: the little hook under the c (ç) makes it sound like *s*.

- **Bonne nuit** means *good night* only when someone goes to bed. Don't use it as a greeting in the evening: say [[Bonsoir]].
- **Salut with a stranger** sounds too casual. With your boss or a clerk, say [[Bonjour]].
- **“Et tu ?”** is wrong. After *et*, say [[Et toi ?]] (or [[Et vous ?]]).
- **“I'm good”**: don't translate word for word. Answer [[Ça va !]] or [[Très bien, merci.]]

In French-speaking places, **saying hello is not optional.** Before you ask anything (in a shop, at a counter, on the bus), start with [[Bonjour]] or [[Bonjour, madame / monsieur]]. Asking a question without it can sound rude.

Friends often greet each other with *la bise* (a light kiss on each cheek), in France and in Québec. With new people and at work, a handshake is normal.

A few things you will hear in Québec and other French-speaking parts of Canada:

- You'll often hear [[Bonjour !]] as a **goodbye** too, when you leave a shop: there it means “have a good day”. This varies from person to person.
- [[Bonne journée !]] (have a nice day) and [[Bonne soirée !]] (have a nice evening) are very common goodbyes.
- [[Allô !]] is how people answer the phone, and also a friendly *hi*.
- When you say [[merci]], you will often hear [[Bienvenue !]], which here means **you're welcome**. [[De rien.]] is also common, and it is what people usually say in France.
- In Montréal shops you may hear [[Bonjour, hi !]]: the clerk lets you choose French or English. Answer [[Bonjour !]] and you will get French.
- **Tu** is used more often and more quickly in Québec than in France, even at work. Still, start with **vous** with strangers and older people.

blocks.title: Listen and repeat
blocks.note: Repeat each line out loud. Record yourself and compare with the model.

lines.tip: No n sound at the end of bon-: it's a nasal vowel.
soir sounds like “swahr”, with a soft throat r.
The t of comment links to allez: “ko-man-ta-lay-voo”.
Make your voice go up for the question.
au = “oh”. bientôt = “byan-toh”, with no n sound.

blocks.prompt: It's 8 p.m. You walk into a restaurant and greet the waitress. You say…
blocks.explain: When you arrive in the evening, use bonsoir. Add madame to be polite.
optionFeedback: Bonne nuit is only for bedtime.
Salut is for friends, and it doesn't go with madame.

blocks.explain: The polite question is Comment allez-vous ?
merci = thank you; madame = madam (no capital letter).

blocks.prompt: Match the French and the English.

blocks.explain: To one friend: s'il te plaît. To a stranger or a group: s'il vous plaît.

blocks.prompt: Very well, thank you. And you? (formal)
blocks.explain: Formal → Et vous ? (Et toi ? is for a friend.)
Ça va ? is the informal “how are you?”.
[[monsieur]] is spelled with -sieur, but sounds like “muh-syuh”.
[[à]] has a grave accent, [[bientôt]] has a circumflex on the o.

blocks.prompt: Who is the speaker probably talking to?
blocks.explain: [[Comment allez-vous ?]] uses vous: it is the polite question.

blocks.prompt: It's morning. You arrive at the front desk of a community centre. Greet the receptionist politely, ask how she is, answer her, thank her and say goodbye.
checklist: Merci + a goodbye (Au revoir / À bientôt / Bonne journée)

models.label: Model answer (polite)
models.fr: Bonjour, madame ! Comment allez-vous ? … Très bien, merci. … Merci, madame. Au revoir, bonne journée !
models.en: Hello, madam! How are you? … Very well, thank you. … Thank you, madam. Goodbye, have a nice day!

models.label: Same thing with a friend
models.fr: Salut, Sofia ! Ça va ? … Ça va bien, merci. Et toi ? … Salut, à bientôt !
models.en: Hi, Sofia! How's it going? … I'm good, thanks. And you? … Bye, see you soon!

blocks.prompt: Write two tiny exchanges of 2–3 lines each: one with a neighbour you don't know well (vous), and one with a friend (tu).
checklist: A polite greeting with madame or monsieur

models.label: Model answer
models.fr:
Bonjour, monsieur. Comment allez-vous ? — Très bien, merci. Et vous ?
Salut, Mei ! Ça va ? — Ça va, merci. Et toi ?
models.en:
Hello, sir. How are you? — Very well, thank you. And you?
Hi, Mei! How's it going? — Fine, thanks. And you?

summary:
- Greet people with [[bonjour]], [[bonsoir]] or [[salut]], and leave with [[au revoir]] or [[à bientôt]]
- Say [[merci]] and [[s'il vous plaît]] / [[s'il te plaît]]
- Ask [[Ça va ?]] or [[Comment allez-vous ?]] and answer [[Très bien, merci. Et vous ?]]
- Choose **tu** for a friend and **vous** for politeness or a group
